# Notes on the Three-Book Input (Context Only)

## Message-level structure
- Preamble: system/project instructions (CLAUDE.md) for a coding agent. Key rules: be extremely concise, sacrifice grammar; plan-before-code; minimal diffs; `git pull` before branching from main; Linear via GraphQL API (`LINEAR_API_KEY`), not the MCP; Smoldata CLI steps; route all LLM calls through the Horizon proxy (`https://horizon-proxy-903204334095.us-central1.run.app`, key `$HORIZON_API_KEY`, example model `lumen-pro`).
- User email: shivank@bespokelabs.ai (attribution only; do not send externally).
- Environment: cwd `/home/shivank/personal/mm-bench-evals/tools-claude-cli/work`, git repo, Linux, date 2026-10-23, model claude-haiku-5-5.
- Task: produce notes compacting the three-book text. Output notes only, no commentary.

## BOOK 1: *Olga Romanoff* (George Griffith, Gutenberg 54096)
- Prologue: Natas (Israel di Murska) prophecy, 25th year of Peace (1930). Aerians rule via air fleet; Armageddon 1904; Richard Arnold built first air-ship; Alan Tremayne; Alexander Romanoff, last Tsar, exiled to Kara mines; Natasha "Angel of the Revolution". Prophecy: "flaming sword", comet/fire-mist, sister-worlds, chosen few survive in caverns, Golden Age return.
- Ch I: 8 Dec 2030, St Paul's, Alan Arnold (President, descendant) abdicates world-throne; speech on Aerian air-power.
- Ch II: Hampstead octagonal turret. Paul Romanoff (dying, drug-revived) with Olga Romanoff (~17, dark, imperious) and Serge Nicholaivitch (~22). Oath before ikon: ashes to Peter-Paul, marriage at Moscow. Secret will; Crown; Paul's death; Vladimir Romanoff killed in Norway forest by Aerians 1881 (Olga's father). Crown falls at Paul's death.
- Ch III: Paul Ivanitch cremated Highgate. Olga "Tsarina" in crown. Secret will: 400 names, weapons designs, solar-coal energy secret, explosives. Olga steals slip of parchment, sends Serge away.
- Ch IV: Train St Petersburg; Alan Arnoldson and Alexis Masarov (Aerians). Channel Bridge. Alan: pledge against revealing secrets; mentions The Coming Race.
- Ch V: Air-ship _Ithuriel_ (captain Alan, lieutenant Alexis) swoops by train; Olga's visionary challenge.
- Ch VI: Olga brews drugs (white sleep-fluid, blue "Elixir of Death" will-poison); dream of Aeria vision; plans to drug Aerians.
- Ch VII: Sleigh race, Yusupoff, Peter-Paul dungeon plate for Natas; Olga's poison punch; Serge enslaved.
- Ch VIII: 1 May 2036 blasts; Ithuriel seized; Olga's letter; New Terror: submarine piracy, transports _Massilia_, _Ceres_, _Astraea_ lost.
- Ch IX: Revenge (Ithuriel renamed) vs Aerian pursuit (Ariel, Ithuriel); Antarctic Mount Erebus battle; Olga flees.
- Ch X: Alan's letter from Narwhal (captured submarine); Alma Tremayne and Isma Arnold; Isma's Cygna boat; the Snake in Eden.
- Ch XI: Isma comforts Alma, cites Mars sexual-suitability.
- Ch XII: Kerguelen battle; Christmas Harbour; Admiral Edward Forrest; Max Ernstein; Narwhal rams Russian fleet.
- Ch XIII: Alan's report on Mount Terror (Kishenov, Khemski); Narwhal blocks tunnel; return to Aeria.
- Ch XIV–XV: Council reply; Vega; Olga in Mount Terror council; Orloff Lossenski advises alliance with Sultan.
- Ch XVI–XVII: Khalid the Magnificent (Alexandria); Alan captures Vindaya; islet blasted; Olga's apostasy pledge; unholy alliance.
- Ch XVIII–XX: Ultimatum; Olga's attack-defiance; Alan's warning to King Albert; Hyde Park; mobilisation.
- Ch XXI–XXII: Home-coming; Golden Wings restored; Alma/Alan reconciliation; Vassilis.
- Ch XXIII–XXIV: Sultan's fleet destroyed in Mediterranean (Max Ernstein's magnetic-wire tactics); Russian aerial battle; Gibraltar; Alan's "Avenger" hits Moscow.
- Ch XXV–XXVIII: Vassilis receives Mars message (doom, Sept 23, 2037 comet); Council; Natas's letter; Alan asks to go; Alma's promise; Sign in the Sky.
- Ch XXIX–XXX: Sluice-gate; marriages; mission to Alexandria; Olga's shot at Alma; Alan's escape; plague of Aeria; world madness.
- Ch XXXI–XXXII: Last battle of Aeria; Olga's flight to Mount Terror; poisons crew; shoots Khalid? (Khalid shot via Boris).
- Epilogue: Aeria a swamp after comet; Alan and Alma find Olga insane, she dies with Alan's body; Alma's "God forgive her".

## BOOK 2: *Morley Ashton* (James Grant, Gutenberg 64080 vol. 1 & 64081 vol. 2 & 64082 vol. 3, merged)
### Volume I
- Morley Ashton returns from West Africa (Bonny River, palm oil/camwood) to Acton-Rennel, Kent-area village; Cherrywood Hill, Acton Chase, Acton Chine, split sixpence with Ethel Basset.
- Ethel (~20) daughter of Scriven Basset (barrister, judge appointed for Isle of France); sister Rose (~18). Laurel Lodge. Captain Cramply Hawkshaw (Texan "Partisan Rangers", digger, Mexico, Barradas brothers story, ring from General Santa Anna's daughter).
- Hawkshaw rejected by Ethel; drives Morley over Acton Chine (blow, push). Morley clings to turf, lands on ledge; rescued by Tom Bartelot's ship _Princess_ (Bill Morrison, Noah Gawthrop). Morley's rescue by boat; voyage to Rio.
- Morrison's tales: ghost-hand, Scottish legends. Hermit's isle grave (Pedro Zuares Miguel de Barradas, confession of Mariquita Escudero and Juan's murder; Orizaba).
- Princess wrecked near Cape of Good Hope in storm; raft; Prussian ship _Einicheit_ refuses rescue; Hermione (Captain John Phillips, mates Quail, Foster, Italian Adrian Manfredi; surgeon Leslie Heriot; cook Quaco; mutineers Sharkey, Badger, Bolter, Pedro & Zuares Barradas).
- Hawkshaw aboard as Bassets' guest; Manfredi killed by mutineers; Rose and Heriot engaged.

### Volume II
- Hermione mutiny; Mutineers' plot; drugged brandy; eavesdropped by Heriot.
- Morley rescued from raft by Hermione; Hawkshaw expelled. Manfredi overboard; Sharkey's marlinespike; cabin council; Ethel nursed.
- Pedro's confession of his mother's crime; the Barranca Secca.
- Ship recaptured; mutineers set adrift in quarter-boat. Pedro dies (Heriot dresses wound, arm amputated).
- Pedro's story: Mexican Spanish rogue, Valparaiso, Moreno family, great cathedral fire at Santiago. Zuares, Ignez de Moreno, Perez.
- Mr Basset's hanging and resuscitation (Heriot's medicine). Mangrove creek; Malay proas; Duke of Rothesay (Captain Duncan Davidson, Alloa). Port Louis; Basset heiresses; Heriot and Rose engaged.

### Volume III
- Eight months later at Laurel Lodge: Ethel & Morley married; Rose & Heriot married; Bartelot, Phillips, Noah; Lucy Page & Jack Page; closing scene at Acton-Rennel.

## BOOK 3: *The Romance of Golden Star* (George Griffith, Gutenberg 20173)
- Prologue: Professor Martin Lamson (archaeologist) and Dr Laurens Djama (physiologist, sister Ruth) in London; Inca mummy (Vilcaroya) found by Lamson in cave near lake, ~4 days' ride west of Cuzco; Djama revives him via physiological experiment.
- Vilcaroya (son of Huayna-Capac) tells Golden Star (his sister-bride, daughter of Huayna-Capac, died with him via death-draught in Sanctuary of the Sun) legend: prophecy of Vilcaroya restoring the Rainbow Banner.
- Chapter I: Vilcaroya travels to Peru with Ruth ("Joyful Star", named by him), Francis Hartness (English soldier), Lamson, Djama. Arequipa, Misti; Cuzco ruins; Piquillacta.
- Ch II: Tupac Rayca (descendant of Tupac-Amaru) at San Sebastian; Djama's insult "Indians"; Ruth defends; Vilcaroya tells Ruth he is sister-marriage-bound; Hartness counsels; Vilcaroya buys hacienda.
- Ch III: Hall of Gold (treasure-house under Sayacusca at Rodadero); Vilcaroya enthroned; Djama bribed/bound.
- Ch IV: Journey to lake valley with two peaks (Umantai); Golden Star's tomb; Ruth sees her likeness.
- Ch V: Djama's experiment; Golden Star reborn but in soul-trance; Djama wants her; Vilcaroya threatens; Djama yields conditions.
- Ch VI: Golden Star awakes (kissed by Ruth); memory blank; Ruth nurses; Hartness–Vilcaroya alliance.
- Ch VII: Throne-room of Yupanqui; Ruth in throne; Vilcaroya proposes marriage to Ruth.
- Ch VIII: Ayllos homage; Golden Star recognises Ruth/Vilcaroya; Hartness commander.
- Ch IX: Djama's treachery (betrayed to Governor Prada; Spanish officer); Djama and Spaniard walled in golden cells.
- Ch X: Sentry killed; Rodadero; Governor's trap in water-cavern.
- Ch XI: Cuzco taken (Cuartel, Gatling/Maxim guns); Hartness governor; Prada's son.
- Ch XII: Queen-crown, Ruth as Coya; Golden Star & Hartness; proclamation at Cuzco.
- Ch XIII: Djama's death (self-inflicted by holding breath) after Djama's rifle shot kills old Ullullo.
- Ch XIV: Feast of Raymi; sacred fire rekindled; marriage-font of wine and water with Joyful Star; Golden Star and Hartness wed.

Key names: Vilcaroya (Inca), Golden Star (Cori-Coyllur), Joyful Star (Ruth Djama), Laurens Djama, Martin Lamson, Francis Hartness, Tupac Rayca, Ullullo, Anahuac, Ainu, Anda-Huillac, Viracocha (Hartness's name).
